title: Optimization of saline wastewater treatment using electrochemical oxidation process: Prediction by RSM method
author: Darvishmotevalli, Zarei, et al.

steps.title: Assemble electro‑oxidation reactor
steps.instruction: Construct a rectangular batch reactor of plexiglass with a net volume of 1 L and internal dimensions 15 cm × 6 cm × 16 cm; install two series of parallel iron electrodes (diameter 1.6 cm, length 14 cm) connected by cable and linked to an AC/DC current source.

steps.title: Prepare synthetic saline wastewater
steps.instruction: Dissolve sodium chloride in deionized water to obtain the desired salt concentration (see variable levels below); adjust the solution so that the initial chemical oxygen demand (COD) is 3500 mg L⁻¹ and total organic carbon (TOC) is 2000 mg L⁻¹.

steps.title: Adjust pH of wastewater
steps.instruction: Use 1 N NaOH or 1 N HCl (Merck) to set the pH of the synthetic wastewater to the required level for each experiment.

steps.title: Define experimental variables and levels
steps.instruction: Select three coded levels (‑1, 0, +1) for each independent variable as follows: pH = 4, 6, 8; reaction time = 20, 30, 40 min; salt concentration (g L⁻¹) = 1, 2, 2; voltage (V) = 3, 6, 9.

steps.title: Design experiments using CCD
steps.instruction: Create a central composite design (CCD) comprising a two‑level full factorial (2⁴ = 16 runs), five central‑point replications, and eight star points (2 × 4), giving a total of 29 experiments (N = Na + N0 + Nc). Use Design‑Expert 7 software to generate the run order randomly.

steps.title: Run electro‑oxidation experiments
steps.instruction: For each of the 29 experimental conditions, place 1 L of prepared wastewater in the reactor, set the specified voltage, maintain the designated reaction time, and keep the pH at the target value; then collect the treated sample.

steps.title: Measure COD and TOC after treatment
steps.instruction: Determine the final COD and TOC concentrations (C_f) of each sample using standard analytical methods.

steps.title: Calculate removal efficiencies
steps.instruction: Compute COD or TOC removal percentage with: % removal = [(C_i − C_f) / C_i] × 100, where C_i is the initial concentration (COD = 3500 mg L⁻¹, TOC = 2000 mg L⁻¹).

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Fit a second‑order response surface model (Y = β₀ + ∑β_iX_i + ∑β_iiX_i² + ∑β_ijX_iX_j + e) to the COD and TOC removal data; evaluate model quality with R² and adjusted R², and assess significance with an F‑test (p ≤ 0.05).

steps.title: Determine optimal conditions
steps.instruction: Using the fitted model, identify the combination of pH, reaction time, salt concentration, and voltage that maximizes COD and TOC removal efficiencies.
